'use client'

import { useState } from 'react'
import { Layout, X, Plus, Trash2, Loader2, AlertCircle } from 'lucide-react'
import { createProjectTemplateAction } from '@/app/(dashboard)/settings/templates/actions'

interface NewTemplateModalProps {
  isOpen: boolean
  onClose: () => void
  onSuccess?: () => void
}

interface TaskDraft {
  title: string
  description?: string
  priority: 'low' | 'medium' | 'high' | 'urgent'
  day_offset: number
}

export function NewTemplateModal({ isOpen, onClose, onSuccess }: NewTemplateModalProps) {
  const [name, setName] = useState('')
  const [description, setDescription] = useState('')
  const [type, setType] = useState('Combined')
  const [defaultAmount, setDefaultAmount] = useState('')
  const [currency, setCurrency] = useState('USD')
  const [deliverablesText, setDeliverablesText] = useState('')
  const [tasks, setTasks] = useState<TaskDraft[]>([
    { title: 'Project Kickoff & Requirements Review', priority: 'high', day_offset: 1 },
    { title: 'Architecture & Design Specification', priority: 'medium', day_offset: 3 }
  ])

  const [isSubmitting, setIsSubmitting] = useState(false)
  const [errorMsg, setErrorMsg] = useState('')

  if (!isOpen) return null

  const handleAddTask = () => {
    setTasks([...tasks, { title: '', priority: 'medium', day_offset: 5 }])
  }

  const handleRemoveTask = (index: number) => {
    setTasks(tasks.filter((_, idx) => idx !== index))
  }

  const handleTaskChange = (index: number, field: keyof TaskDraft, value: any) => {
    const updated = [...tasks]
    updated[index] = { ...updated[index], [field]: value }
    setTasks(updated)
  }

  const handleSubmit = async (e: React.FormEvent) => {
    e.preventDefault()
    if (!name.trim()) {
      setErrorMsg('Template name is required.')
      return
    }

    const validTasks = tasks.filter((t) => t.title.trim() !== '')

    setIsSubmitting(true)
    setErrorMsg('')
    try {
      const formData = new FormData()
      formData.append('name', name)
      formData.append('description', description)
      formData.append('type', type)
      formData.append('default_amount', defaultAmount)
      formData.append('currency', currency)
      formData.append('default_deliverables', deliverablesText)
      formData.append('tasks_json', JSON.stringify(validTasks))

      const res = await createProjectTemplateAction(formData)
      if (res.success) {
        onClose()
        if (onSuccess) onSuccess()
      } else {
        setErrorMsg(res.error || 'Failed to create template')
      }
    } catch (err: any) {
      setErrorMsg(err.message || 'Error creating template')
    } finally {
      setIsSubmitting(false)
    }
  }

  return (
    <div className="fixed inset-0 z-50 flex items-center justify-center bg-slate-950/70 backdrop-blur-sm p-4 animate-in fade-in duration-200">
      <div className="w-full max-w-2xl bg-white dark:bg-slate-900 border border-slate-200 dark:border-slate-800 rounded-2xl shadow-xl overflow-hidden">
        {/* Header */}
        <div className="flex items-center justify-between p-5 border-b border-slate-200 dark:border-slate-800 bg-slate-50 dark:bg-slate-800/50">
          <div className="flex items-center gap-2">
            <Layout className="w-5 h-5 text-indigo-600 dark:text-indigo-400" />
            <h2 className="font-bold text-slate-900 dark:text-white text-base">
              Create Project Template
            </h2>
          </div>
          <button
            onClick={onClose}
            className="p-1 text-slate-400 hover:text-slate-600 dark:hover:text-slate-200 transition"
          >
            <X className="w-5 h-5" />
          </button>
        </div>

        {/* Form Body */}
        <form onSubmit={handleSubmit} className="p-6 space-y-4 max-h-[75vh] overflow-y-auto pr-2 text-xs">
          {errorMsg && (
            <div className="p-3 bg-red-500/10 border border-red-500/20 rounded-xl text-xs text-red-600 dark:text-red-400 flex items-center gap-2">
              <AlertCircle className="w-4 h-4 shrink-0" />
              <span>{errorMsg}</span>
            </div>
          )}

          <div className="grid grid-cols-1 sm:grid-cols-2 gap-3">
            <div>
              <label className="block font-semibold text-slate-700 dark:text-slate-300 mb-1">
                Template Name *
              </label>
              <input
                type="text"
                required
                placeholder="e.g. AI Voice Agent Standard Workflow"
                value={name}
                onChange={(e) => setName(e.target.value)}
                className="w-full px-3 py-2 bg-slate-50 dark:bg-slate-800 border border-slate-200 dark:border-slate-700 rounded-lg text-sm text-slate-900 dark:text-white focus:outline-hidden focus:ring-2 focus:ring-indigo-500"
              />
            </div>

            <div>
              <label className="block font-semibold text-slate-700 dark:text-slate-300 mb-1">
                Project Type
              </label>
              <select
                value={type}
                onChange={(e) => setType(e.target.value)}
                className="w-full px-3 py-2 bg-slate-50 dark:bg-slate-800 border border-slate-200 dark:border-slate-700 rounded-lg text-xs text-slate-900 dark:text-white focus:outline-hidden focus:ring-2 focus:ring-indigo-500"
              >
                <option value="AI Voice Agent">AI Voice Agent</option>
                <option value="UGC Media">UGC Media</option>
                <option value="Automation">Automation</option>
                <option value="Combined">Combined</option>
              </select>
            </div>
          </div>

          <div className="grid grid-cols-1 sm:grid-cols-2 gap-3">
            <div>
              <label className="block font-semibold text-slate-700 dark:text-slate-300 mb-1">
                Default Contract Amount
              </label>
              <input
                type="number"
                placeholder="5000"
                value={defaultAmount}
                onChange={(e) => setDefaultAmount(e.target.value)}
                className="w-full px-3 py-2 bg-slate-50 dark:bg-slate-800 border border-slate-200 dark:border-slate-700 rounded-lg text-xs text-slate-900 dark:text-white focus:outline-hidden focus:ring-2 focus:ring-indigo-500"
              />
            </div>

            <div>
              <label className="block font-semibold text-slate-700 dark:text-slate-300 mb-1">
                Currency
              </label>
              <select
                value={currency}
                onChange={(e) => setCurrency(e.target.value)}
                className="w-full px-3 py-2 bg-slate-50 dark:bg-slate-800 border border-slate-200 dark:border-slate-700 rounded-lg text-xs text-slate-900 dark:text-white focus:outline-hidden focus:ring-2 focus:ring-indigo-500"
              >
                <option value="USD">USD ($)</option>
                <option value="EUR">EUR (€)</option>
                <option value="GBP">GBP (£)</option>
              </select>
            </div>
          </div>

          <div>
            <label className="block font-semibold text-slate-700 dark:text-slate-300 mb-1">
              Description
            </label>
            <textarea
              rows={2}
              placeholder="Standard deliverables and execution guide..."
              value={description}
              onChange={(e) => setDescription(e.target.value)}
              className="w-full px-3 py-2 bg-slate-50 dark:bg-slate-800 border border-slate-200 dark:border-slate-700 rounded-lg text-sm text-slate-900 dark:text-white focus:outline-hidden focus:ring-2 focus:ring-indigo-500"
            />
          </div>

          <div>
            <label className="block font-semibold text-slate-700 dark:text-slate-300 mb-1">
              Default Deliverables (One per line)
            </label>
            <textarea
              rows={3}
              placeholder="Voice Bot Dialog Flow Diagram&#10;Twilio Audio Webhook Integration&#10;QA Load Test Report"
              value={deliverablesText}
              onChange={(e) => setDeliverablesText(e.target.value)}
              className="w-full px-3 py-2 bg-slate-50 dark:bg-slate-800 border border-slate-200 dark:border-slate-700 rounded-lg text-xs text-slate-900 dark:text-white focus:outline-hidden focus:ring-2 focus:ring-indigo-500"
            />
          </div>

          {/* Pre-configured Tasks Builder */}
          <div className="space-y-3 pt-2 border-t border-slate-200 dark:border-slate-800">
            <div className="flex items-center justify-between">
              <h3 className="font-bold text-slate-900 dark:text-white text-xs uppercase tracking-wider">
                Pre-configured Task Scaffolding ({tasks.length})
              </h3>
              <button
                type="button"
                onClick={handleAddTask}
                className="inline-flex items-center gap-1 text-xs text-indigo-600 dark:text-indigo-400 font-semibold hover:underline"
              >
                <Plus className="w-3.5 h-3.5" /> Add Task Step
              </button>
            </div>

            <div className="space-y-2">
              {tasks.map((t, idx) => (
                <div
                  key={idx}
                  className="p-3 bg-slate-50 dark:bg-slate-800/60 rounded-xl border border-slate-200 dark:border-slate-700 space-y-2"
                >
                  <div className="flex items-center justify-between gap-2">
                    <input
                      type="text"
                      placeholder="Task step title..."
                      value={t.title}
                      onChange={(e) => handleTaskChange(idx, 'title', e.target.value)}
                      className="flex-1 px-2.5 py-1 bg-white dark:bg-slate-900 border border-slate-200 dark:border-slate-700 rounded text-xs text-slate-900 dark:text-white focus:outline-hidden"
                    />
                    <button
                      type="button"
                      onClick={() => handleRemoveTask(idx)}
                      className="p-1 text-red-400 hover:text-red-600 transition"
                    >
                      <Trash2 className="w-3.5 h-3.5" />
                    </button>
                  </div>

                  <div className="grid grid-cols-2 gap-2 text-[11px]">
                    <div>
                      <label className="text-slate-400">Priority:</label>
                      <select
                        value={t.priority}
                        onChange={(e) => handleTaskChange(idx, 'priority', e.target.value)}
                        className="w-full mt-0.5 px-2 py-1 bg-white dark:bg-slate-900 border border-slate-200 dark:border-slate-700 rounded text-slate-900 dark:text-white"
                      >
                        <option value="low">Low</option>
                        <option value="medium">Medium</option>
                        <option value="high">High</option>
                        <option value="urgent">Urgent</option>
                      </select>
                    </div>

                    <div>
                      <label className="text-slate-400">Day Offset (from start):</label>
                      <input
                        type="number"
                        value={t.day_offset}
                        onChange={(e) =>
                          handleTaskChange(idx, 'day_offset', parseInt(e.target.value || '0', 10))
                        }
                        className="w-full mt-0.5 px-2 py-1 bg-white dark:bg-slate-900 border border-slate-200 dark:border-slate-700 rounded text-slate-900 dark:text-white"
                      />
                    </div>
                  </div>
                </div>
              ))}
            </div>
          </div>

          {/* Footer Actions */}
          <div className="flex items-center justify-end gap-3 pt-4 border-t border-slate-100 dark:border-slate-800">
            <button
              type="button"
              onClick={onClose}
              className="px-4 py-2 text-xs font-medium text-slate-600 dark:text-slate-400 hover:text-slate-900 dark:hover:text-white transition"
            >
              Cancel
            </button>
            <button
              type="submit"
              disabled={isSubmitting}
              className="inline-flex items-center gap-2 px-5 py-2 bg-indigo-600 hover:bg-indigo-700 text-white rounded-lg text-xs font-medium transition shadow-xs disabled:opacity-50"
            >
              {isSubmitting && <Loader2 className="w-3.5 h-3.5 animate-spin" />}
              Save Template
            </button>
          </div>
        </form>
      </div>
    </div>
  )
}

--- FILE: components/templates/TemplateList.tsx ---
'use client'

import { useState } from 'react'
import { useRouter } from 'next/navigation'
import {
  Layout,
  Plus,
  Trash2,
  CheckSquare,
  FolderCheck,
  DollarSign,
  Briefcase,
  ChevronDown,
  ChevronUp
} from 'lucide-react'
import { ProjectTemplateRecord, deleteProjectTemplateAction } from '@/app/(dashboard)/settings/templates/actions'
import { NewTemplateModal } from './NewTemplateModal'

interface TemplateListProps {
  initialTemplates: ProjectTemplateRecord[]
}

export function TemplateList({ initialTemplates }: TemplateListProps) {
  const router = useRouter()
  const [templates, setTemplates] = useState<ProjectTemplateRecord[]>(initialTemplates)
  const [isNewModalOpen, setIsNewModalOpen] = useState(false)
  const [expandedId, setExpandedId] = useState<string | null>(null)

  const handleDelete = async (templateId: string) => {
    if (!confirm('Are you sure you want to delete this project template?')) return

    setTemplates((prev) => prev.filter((t) => t.id !== templateId))
    try {
      const res = await deleteProjectTemplateAction(templateId)
      if (!res.success) {
        alert(res.error || 'Failed to delete template')
      }
    } catch (err: any) {
      alert(err.message || 'Error deleting template')
    }
  }

  const formatCurrency = (amount?: number, curr = 'USD') => {
    if (!amount) return '$0'
    return new Intl.NumberFormat('en-US', {
      style: 'currency',
      currency: curr,
      maximumFractionDigits: 0
    }).format(amount)
  }

  return (
    <div className="space-y-6">
      {/* Top Header */}
      <div className="flex flex-col md:flex-row md:items-center md:justify-between gap-4">
        <div>
          <h1 className="text-2xl font-bold text-slate-900 dark:text-white flex items-center gap-2">
            <Layout className="w-7 h-7 text-indigo-600 dark:text-indigo-400" />
            Project Templates Library
          </h1>
          <p className="text-sm text-slate-500 dark:text-slate-400 mt-1">
            Save recurring project structures as reusable templates with task scaffolding and deliverables.
          </p>
        </div>

        <button
          onClick={() => setIsNewModalOpen(true)}
          className="inline-flex items-center justify-center gap-2 px-4 py-2.5 bg-indigo-600 hover:bg-indigo-700 text-white rounded-lg font-medium text-sm transition shadow-sm"
        >
          <Plus className="w-4 h-4" />
          Create Template
        </button>
      </div>

      {/* Templates Grid */}
      {templates.length === 0 ? (
        <div className="text-center py-12 bg-white dark:bg-slate-900 rounded-xl border border-slate-200 dark:border-slate-800">
          <Layout className="mx-auto h-12 w-12 text-slate-400 dark:text-slate-600" />
          <h3 className="mt-2 text-sm font-semibold text-slate-900 dark:text-white">
            No templates created yet
          </h3>
          <p className="mt-1 text-sm text-slate-500 dark:text-slate-400">
            Build reusable project templates to scaffold tasks and deliverables automatically.
          </p>
          <div className="mt-6">
            <button
              onClick={() => setIsNewModalOpen(true)}
              className="inline-flex items-center gap-2 px-4 py-2 bg-indigo-600 hover:bg-indigo-700 text-white rounded-lg text-sm font-medium transition"
            >
              <Plus className="w-4 h-4" />
              Create Template
            </button>
          </div>
        </div>
      ) : (
        <div className="grid grid-cols-1 md:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-3 gap-6">
          {templates.map((tmpl) => {
            const taskCount = tmpl.tasks?.length || 0
            const deliverableCount = tmpl.default_deliverables?.length || 0
            const isExpanded = expandedId === tmpl.id

            return (
              <div
                key={tmpl.id}
                className="bg-white dark:bg-slate-900 border border-slate-200 dark:border-slate-800 rounded-2xl p-5 shadow-xs flex flex-col justify-between space-y-4 hover:border-slate-300 dark:hover:border-slate-700 transition"
              >
                <div className="space-y-3">
                  <div className="flex items-start justify-between gap-2">
                    <div className="space-y-1">
                      <span className="inline-block text-[11px] font-semibold px-2 py-0.5 rounded-md bg-indigo-500/10 text-indigo-600 dark:text-indigo-400 border border-indigo-500/20">
                        {tmpl.type || 'Combined'}
                      </span>
                      <h3 className="font-bold text-base text-slate-900 dark:text-white">
                        {tmpl.name}
                      </h3>
                    </div>

                    <button
                      onClick={() => handleDelete(tmpl.id)}
                      className="p-1 text-red-400 hover:text-red-600 transition"
                      title="Delete Template"
                    >
                      <Trash2 className="w-4 h-4" />
                    </button>
                  </div>

                  {tmpl.description && (
                    <p className="text-xs text-slate-500 dark:text-slate-400 line-clamp-2">
                      {tmpl.description}
                    </p>
                  )}

                  {/* Template Meta Info */}
                  <div className="grid grid-cols-3 gap-2 py-3 border-y border-slate-100 dark:border-slate-800 text-center text-xs">
                    <div>
                      <div className="text-[10px] text-slate-400 uppercase font-semibold">Value</div>
                      <div className="font-bold text-slate-900 dark:text-white mt-0.5">
                        {formatCurrency(tmpl.default_amount, tmpl.currency)}
                      </div>
                    </div>

                    <div>
                      <div className="text-[10px] text-slate-400 uppercase font-semibold">Tasks</div>
                      <div className="font-bold text-slate-900 dark:text-white mt-0.5">
                        {taskCount} steps
                      </div>
                    </div>

                    <div>
                      <div className="text-[10px] text-slate-400 uppercase font-semibold">Files</div>
                      <div className="font-bold text-slate-900 dark:text-white mt-0.5">
                        {deliverableCount} items
                      </div>
                    </div>
                  </div>
                </div>

                {/* Expandable Task & Deliverable Drawer */}
                <div className="space-y-2">
                  <button
                    onClick={() => setExpandedId(isExpanded ? null : tmpl.id)}
                    className="w-full flex items-center justify-between text-xs font-semibold text-slate-600 dark:text-slate-400 hover:text-slate-900 dark:hover:text-white transition"
                  >
                    <span>View Template Details</span>
                    {isExpanded ? <ChevronUp className="w-4 h-4" /> : <ChevronDown className="w-4 h-4" />}
                  </button>

                  {isExpanded && (
                    <div className="p-3 bg-slate-50 dark:bg-slate-800/60 rounded-xl space-y-3 text-xs border border-slate-200/60 dark:border-slate-800">
                      {/* Tasks list */}
                      <div>
                        <div className="font-semibold text-slate-900 dark:text-white mb-1 flex items-center gap-1.5">
                          <CheckSquare className="w-3.5 h-3.5 text-indigo-500" />
                          Pre-configured Tasks:
                        </div>
                        {taskCount === 0 ? (
                          <div className="text-slate-400 text-[11px]">No tasks defined</div>
                        ) : (
                          <ul className="space-y-1 pl-4 list-disc text-slate-600 dark:text-slate-400 text-[11px]">
                            {tmpl.tasks?.map((t) => (
                              <li key={t.id}>
                                <span className="font-medium text-slate-800 dark:text-slate-200">{t.title}</span> (Day {t.day_offset})
                              </li>
                            ))}
                          </ul>
                        )}
                      </div>

                      {/* Deliverables list */}
                      <div>
                        <div className="font-semibold text-slate-900 dark:text-white mb-1 flex items-center gap-1.5">
                          <FolderCheck className="w-3.5 h-3.5 text-emerald-500" />
                          Default Deliverables:
                        </div>
                        {deliverableCount === 0 ? (
                          <div className="text-slate-400 text-[11px]">No deliverables defined</div>
                        ) : (
                          <ul className="space-y-1 pl-4 list-disc text-slate-600 dark:text-slate-400 text-[11px]">
                            {tmpl.default_deliverables.map((del, idx) => (
                              <li key={idx}>{del}</li>
                            ))}
                          </ul>
                        )}
                      </div>
                    </div>
                  )}
                </div>
              </div>
            )
          })}
        </div>
      )}

      {/* New Template Modal */}
      {isNewModalOpen && (
        <NewTemplateModal
          isOpen={isNewModalOpen}
          onClose={() => setIsNewModalOpen(false)}
          onSuccess={() => {
            setIsNewModalOpen(false)
            router.refresh()
          }}
        />
      )}
    </div>
  )
}

## Critical Decisions & Context
- Multi-tenancy model: Shared DB + Schema with `organization_id` foreign keys + Supabase RLS.
- Settings & Role Security: All team role modifications, member removals, and org profile edits are role-gated server-side (only `owner` or `admin`). Last owner removal or demotion is blocked.
- Reusable Project Templates: `project_templates` and `project_template_tasks` schema with day-offsets, default deliverables, and automatic task/deliverable scaffolding upon project instantiation.
- Client Communication Mode: Clients support `manual` and `connected` modes. Strict one-way promotion (`manual` -> `connected`) is enforced permanently. In `connected` mode, webhook ingestion auto-matches messages by email/phone into unified inbox; in `manual` mode, incoming messages are never auto-matched and communication views show only manual records.
- AI Feature Architecture: Provider-agnostic shared layer (`lib/ai/client.ts`) supporting OpenAI, Anthropic Claude, Google Gemini, and a deterministic Mock provider. Dual-gating enforced via Super Admin kill switch (`platform_settings.global_feature_flags.ai_kill_switch`) and tenant subscription plan limits (`subscription_plans.feature_limits.ai_features_enabled`). Centralized prompt templates in `lib/ai/prompts/` and per-tenant usage accounting in `ai_usage_log`.
- AI Inbox Reply Suggestions: Context-aware suggestions analyzing up to 6 recent thread messages into 3 tone options (Professional, Collaborative, Direct/Concise). Strictly human-in-the-loop (never auto-sends). Mode-aware: connected mode offers 1-click send via channel or edit in draft; manual mode offers draft editing and clipboard copy. Dual-tier gating enforced: AI-disabled organizations render no button at all.
- AI Lead Scoring in CRM Pipeline: Deal cards in `/leads` and `/clients/[id]/pipeline` display an objective 0–100 AI Score badge with color coding (0–33 Red: Low Quality, 34–66 Yellow: Medium Potential, 67–100 Green: High-Quality Prospect). Evaluates 4 dimensions: Deal Value, Stage Progression Velocity, Client Engagement (from `communication_messages`), and Project History (completed vs overdue from `projects`). Clicking the badge opens `LeadScoreBreakdownModal` with a circular score gauge, executive rationale, factor impact cards, recommended action, and on-demand re-score. Header includes 1-click batch re-score. Strict dual-tier gating omits all score badges and buttons when AI is disabled. Lead scores are assistive signals only and never automatically transition pipeline stages. All scoring requests are accounted in `ai_usage_log`.
- AI Auto-Task Extraction from Messages: Interactive task extraction available on message threads in `/inbox` and `/clients/[id]/communications`. Evaluates message content for actionable requests, deliverables, and deadlines, extracting candidate tasks with title, context description, calculated due date, suggested assignee role, and confidence score (0–100%). Strictly human-in-the-loop: candidate tasks are presented in `TaskExtractionModal` via `SuggestedTaskCard`, allowing project selection (pre-selecting the client's active project) and assignee configuration prior to creation. Tasks are never auto-created silently. Creation inserts rows into `public.tasks`, attributes source snippet context, and logs `TASK_CREATED` audit events. Dual-tier gating enforced (platform kill switch + plan limit): zero-button rule applied when disabled. All invocations logged in `ai_usage_log`.
- AI Weekly Report Narratives: Pure feature orchestrator `generateWeeklyReportNarrative` synthesizing 6 business metrics (completed tasks, active projects, new clients, revenue, communication volume, overdue items) into an executive Markdown narrative report. Strict anti-fabrication prompt ensures 100% metric fidelity with zero invented numbers. "Generate Weekly Report" action available on `/dashboard` and dedicated `/reports` page. Provides `WeeklyReportModal` with 6 metric badges, inline Markdown editing, print/PDF export styling, and stakeholder email sharing. Zero-button rule enforced when AI is disabled. Pluggable for automated n8n/Slack cron (Task 52) and Analytics (Task 58). All invocations recorded in `ai_usage_log`.
- AI Settings & Usage Controls: Per-organization AI feature toggles stored in `organizations.ai_feature_settings` (JSONB) with full tenant administration. Enforces three-tier gating hierarchy: (1) Platform kill switch & feature flags (`platform_settings`), (2) Subscription tier plan limits (`subscription_plans.feature_limits`), (3) Organization-level feature toggles. Tenant admins and owners can toggle 4 independent capabilities: `reply_suggestions`, `lead_scoring`, `task_extraction`, and `weekly_narrative`. Dedicated UI at `/settings/ai` surfaces live monthly consumption metrics (total requests, token volume, estimated cost) aggregated from `ai_usage_log`, alongside granular capability cards with active/disabled badges and switch controls. All configuration changes log `AI_FEATURE_TOGGLE_UPDATED` audit events.
- N8N Automation Architecture & Webhook Contracts: Defined event contract and signed outbound webhook sender (`lib/automation/emitter.ts`) for the self-hosted n8n instance on Contabo VPS (`n8n.innoventixhub.com`). Tenant organizations configure `automation_webhook_url` and `automation_webhook_secret` (Migration `0024_organization_automation_webhooks.sql`) with environment fallback. All payloads (`project.delivered`, `task.deadline_approaching`, `project.overdue`, `weekly.summary_ready`) are signed via HMAC-SHA256 (`X-Automation-Signature: sha256=<hex>`), including unique delivery ID and ISO timestamp. Inbound verification route available at `/api/automation/events`. Full architecture and n8n Code node verification scripts documented in `documentation/automation-contracts.md`.
- Automation: Project Delivered -> Invoice Trigger: Implemented N8N Flow 1 connecting Project Management to Invoice Automation. On project status transition to `delivered`, server action evaluates client billing schedule (`payment_schedule === 'per_project'`). If per-project, updates `delivered_at`, flags `invoice_triggered = true`, emits signed `project.delivered` event, and logs `PROJECT_DELIVERED_INVOICE_TRIGGERED`. Confirmed callback route at `/api/automation/callback/invoice-created` validates HMAC signature, updates status to `invoiced`, and logs audit trail. UI integration delivers `DeliverProjectConfirmModal` in both project detail header (`ProjectHeader.tsx`) and Kanban board (`ProjectsKanban.tsx`). Full workflow export provided in `n8n/workflows/project-delivered-invoice.json`.
- Automation: Deadline & Overdue Alerts: Implemented N8N Flow 2 (Task Due Tomorrow Alert) and Flow 3 (Project Overdue Alert) triggered via daily cron route at `/api/automation/cron/deadline-check`. Scoped per organization with secret-header protection (`x-cron-secret` / `Authorization: Bearer`). Idempotent deduplication query checks `in_app_notifications` to prevent duplicate daily alert dispatch for identical entities. Emits signed `task.deadline_approaching` and `project.overdue` events to n8n and stores in-app notifications. Complete n8n workflows provided in `n8n/workflows/task-deadline-alert.json` and `n8n/workflows/project-overdue-alert.json`.
- Automation: Weekly Summary Report: Implemented N8N Flow 4 scheduled for Monday 9:00 AM via cron route `/api/automation/cron/weekly-summary`. Aggregates 6 key multi-tenant operational figures: completed tasks, active projects, new clients, delivered/invoiced revenue, communication message volume, and overdue items across the trailing 7 days. If AI narrative capability is permitted by the 3-tier gating check (`checkAIAccess`), generates an executive narrative via `generateWeeklyReportNarrative`; otherwise cleanly omits the narrative while preserving metric integrity. Emits signed `weekly.summary_ready` event to n8n for Slack distribution to `#leadership` and writes in-app notification record. Full workflow export provided in `n8n/workflows/weekly-summary.json`.
- N8N Workflow Activation on Contabo VPS (Task 69): Comprehensive deployment documentation at `documentation/infra/n8n-deployment.md` covering import steps (Web UI and CLI methods), credentials/config (Slack OAuth with required scopes, `AUTOMATION_WEBHOOK_SECRET` matching, `NODE_FUNCTION_ALLOW_BUILTIN=crypto`), webhook contract verification matrix, activation procedures, and manual test procedures with signed `curl` examples for all 4 workflows. **Critical bugfix**: Discovered and resolved that `emitAutomationEvent` was sending all events to a single `N8N_WEBHOOK_URL` path, but each n8n workflow listens on a separate webhook path. Added `EVENT_WEBHOOK_PATHS` mapping in `lib/automation/emitter.ts` that maps event names to specific n8n webhook paths (e.g., `project.delivered` → `/webhook/project-delivered`). Updated `.env.production.example` to use base URL (`https://n8n.innoventixhub.com`) instead of `/webhook/events`. Build: ✅ 0 errors.






- Client Portal Auth & RLS (Task 54): Implemented fully isolated second auth boundary. `client_users` table links Supabase auth identities to `clients` rows (separate from `organization_members`). Magic-link login at `/client/login` via Supabase OTP (`shouldCreateUser: false` — prevents unauthorized account creation). Portal auth callback at `/client/auth/callback` validates `client_users` record before granting session. Three RLS helper functions: `get_portal_client_id()`, `is_portal_user()`, `portal_plan_enabled()`. Scoped read-only RLS policies on `clients`, `projects`, `tasks`, `deliverables` for portal users constrained to their single `client_id` AND org plan gate. `inviteClientToPortal()` and `revokePortalAccess()` server actions in `lib/portal/auth.ts`. `requirePortalSession()` guard for all portal server components. Middleware guards `/client/*` routes. Portal CSS tokens added to globals.css. Migration `0026_client_portal_auth.sql`. Build: ✅ 0 errors.
- Analytics Dashboard (Task 58): Executive analytics overview at `/analytics` delivering Sub-task 7 requirements. Server-side RLS queries compute Revenue Pipeline (active project sum, invoiced vs paid historical), Projects by Status (interactive SVG donut chart with percentages), Team Workload (per-member assigned tasks & capacity bars), Deadlines & Overdue Items (tabbed view with red-highlighted overdue warnings and 7-day upcoming milestones), and Monthly Delivery Velocity (SVG bar chart of completed deliverables & delivered projects across trailing 6 months). Includes Date-Range selector (`30d`, `90d`, `ytd`, `all`) and 1-click AI Executive Briefing button integrating Task 47's narrative synthesizer with 3-tier gating. Build: ✅ 0 errors.
- Revenue & Plan Usage Reporting (Task 59): Extended analytics suite with dedicated sub-routes `/analytics/revenue` and `/analytics/plan-usage`. Computes live resource utilization vs plan limits for team members, clients, projects, storage, connected channels, and monthly AI requests with 4-tier proximity warnings (healthy <80%, warning ≥80%, critical ≥95%, exceeded ≥100%) and upsell prompts. Provides client and project type revenue breakdowns, sortable and filterable ledger tables with client-side CSV and print/PDF export, top client revenue bar charts, monthly trends visualizers (revenue, active projects, closed tasks), and unified sub-tab navigation (`AnalyticsNav`). Integrated live quota cards directly into executive overview (`/analytics`) and billing settings (`/settings/billing`). Build: ✅ 0 errors across 47 routes.
- Client Portal Settings & Preferences (Task 60): Implemented client-facing settings suite at `/client/settings` (and `/portal/settings` redirect). Five tabbed views: (1) Company Profile (name, company, email, phone, country, logo URL preview), (2) Billing & Invoicing (billing email, tax ID/VAT, preferred payment method, PO mandate, automated receipts), (3) Notifications (granular alert toggles for new projects, deliverables ready for review, deadline warnings, invoice issues), (4) Channels & Status (live connection status and sync timestamps for WhatsApp, Slack, Email, and n8n webhooks), (5) Authorized Users (view active portal users for the client account with invitation details). Backed by migration `0027_client_portal_settings.sql` adding `portal_settings` JSONB and RLS self-update and team-view policies. Server actions validate all inputs and revalidate paths. Build: ✅ 0 errors across 49 routes.
- Input Validation & Sanitization Layer (Task 61): Implemented defense-in-depth validation and security layer. Centralized Zod schemas in `lib/validation/schemas.ts` for CRM clients, projects, tasks, deliverables, organizations, team invites, messages, AI triggers, and portal settings. Built XSS neutralization engine in `lib/validation/sanitize.ts` (`sanitizeString`, `escapeHtml`, `sanitizeUrl`, `sanitizeObject`) removing script tags, iframes, and inline event handlers, and strictly gating URL protocols (`http:`, `https:`, `mailto:`). Built `validateAndSanitize` wrapper in `lib/validation/action-wrapper.ts` formatting field errors and scrubbing payloads before DB insertion. Implemented sliding-window rate limiter in `lib/security/rate-limit.ts` with automatic TTL cleanup. Validated across 24 automated unit and security tests in `scripts/test-validation.ts` (0 failures). Build: ✅ 0 errors.
- Secrets Management & API Security (Task 62): Comprehensive backend and API security hardening pass. Enforced AES-256-GCM application-level encryption for all provider tokens (Slack bot tokens/signing secrets, Twilio SIDs/auth tokens, Discord tokens/public keys, SendGrid API keys, Upwork API keys) at rest in `lib/security/encrypt.ts` (`isEncryptedSecret`, `maskSecret`). Enforced strict webhook signature and secret validation across all inbound endpoints: Slack (HMAC-SHA256 with 5m replay prevention), WhatsApp (Twilio signature check with timing-safe byte equality), Discord (pure Ed25519 public key verification via Node crypto), Email & Upwork (channel secret validation), Stripe (constructEvent), and n8n Automation (HMAC-SHA256). Added CORS policy headers and preflight handling (`lib/security/cors.ts`). Built payload size limiter (`lib/security/payload.ts`) rejecting DoS payloads >1MB (413). Implemented sliding-window rate limiter in `middleware/rate-limit.ts` (120 req/min for webhooks/automation, 20 req/min for auth, 60 req/min general). Configured HTTP security headers (`lib/security/headers.ts`: CSP, X-Frame-Options: DENY, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, HSTS) in `middleware.ts`. Audited environment variables confirming zero secrets exposed via `NEXT_PUBLIC_`. Validated across 36 unit/integration security tests in `scratch/test_security_audit.ts`. Build: ✅ 0 errors across 57 routes.
- Audit Logging & Compliance Completeness (Task 63): Implemented immutable, tenant-isolated audit logging system. Created `audit_logs` table (Migration `0028_audit_logs.sql`) with append-only RLS guarantees (`UPDATE` and `DELETE` policies enforce `USING (FALSE)`). Structured taxonomy in `lib/audit/log.ts` covering 30+ actions across Auth, Organization, Team, CRM, Projects, Tasks, Billing, Super Admin, AI, and Automation. Comprehensive query layer (`lib/audit/query.ts`) with tenant-scoped filtering, super-admin platform visibility, search, pagination, and RFC-compliant CSV export (`formatAuditLogsCsv`). Dedicated viewer UI at `/settings/audit-log` for organization owners/admins and `/super-admin/audit-log` for platform super admins. Build: ✅ 0 errors.

  4. Client communication mode transitions (`tests/communication-mode.test.ts` — 5 tests): manual -> connected one-way rule, reversion rejection, idempotent mode updates.

  6. Webhook signature verification (`tests/webhook-verification.test.ts` — 21 tests): cryptographic validation across Slack (HMAC-SHA256, 5m replay window), WhatsApp/Twilio (HMAC-SHA1, sorted params), Discord (Ed25519 public key verification), n8n Automation (HMAC-SHA256), plus ingestion normalizers.

  9. Project templates integration (`tests/integration-project-templates.test.ts` — 3 tests): template scaffolding for tasks with offset due dates and default deliverables, validation, project plan limits.
  10. Client portal auth integration (`tests/integration-portal-auth.test.ts` — 6 tests): magic link invitation flow, session verification, `client_users` lookup, plan gate checks (`client_portal_enabled`).
- Screen Fixes — Prompt 02 Step 1: Removed all developer fallbacks (`getDev*`, `DEV_*`, `__DEV_*`, `DEV_SAMPLE_*`, and `DEV_SUPER_ADMIN` branches) across projects, tasks, inbox, notifications, clients, leads, reports, templates, cron routes, audit logging, and page views. Deleted `app/api/auth/dev-bypass/route.ts` (returns 404 on GET and POST) and `lib/dev/fallbacks.ts`. Empty tenants return clean empty arrays and 0 counts. Verified with 199/199 tests passing and 0 Next.js build errors. Scanner confirms 0 `DEV_FALLBACK` instances remaining.
- Screen Fixes — Prompt 02 Step 2: Multi-tenant isolation enforced in 5 atomic commits (A through E). Scoped project pages users/clients queries; locked `/api/users` and `/api/organizations/[id]` boundaries; eliminated query (`?orgId=`) and body (`organizationId`) overrides across 22 API endpoints using `getTenantOrgId`; gated `setActiveOrgAction` with membership check; scoped portal settings actions; implemented comprehensive cross-tenant regression tests (`tests/step2-commit-e-cross-tenant-isolation.test.ts`). 228/228 unit/integration tests passing (100%), 0 build errors, 0 DEV_FALLBACK, 0 QUERY/BODY overrides. Kept local (not pushed).




--- FILE: .github/workflows/deploy.yml ---
name: CI/CD Pipeline - Build, Test & Deploy to Contabo VPS

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      target_env:
        description: 'Deployment target environment (production or staging)'
        required: true
        default: 'production'
        type: choice
        options:
          - production
          - staging

permissions:
  contents: read
  packages: write

concurrency:
  group: deploy-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  # =========================================================================
  # STEP 1 & 2: VALIDATE (Type Check, Tests, and Next.js Build)
  # =========================================================================
  validate:
    name: Type-Check, Test & Build Validation
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    services:
      postgres:
        image: postgres:16-alpine
        env:
          POSTGRES_USER: postgres
          POSTGRES_PASSWORD: postgres_dev_password
          POSTGRES_DB: innoventix
        ports:
          - 54322:5432
        options: >-
          --health-cmd pg_isready
          --health-interval 10s
          --health-timeout 5s
          --health-retries 5

    steps:
      - name: Checkout Code
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Setup Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20
          cache: 'npm'

      - name: Install Dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Run Type Check (Fail Fast)
        run: npm run type-check

      - name: Run Automated Test Suite (Vitest)
        run: npm run test
        env:
          DATABASE_URL: postgres://postgres:postgres_dev_password@localhost:54322/innoventix
          DB_HOST: localhost
          DB_PORT: 54322
          DB_USER: postgres
          DB_PASSWORD: postgres_dev_password
          DB_NAME: innoventix
          JWT_SECRET: d0a391b9da5876ead44bdbf4de07fa3cf73ebe0355f65521e9b902f256c4851f
          REFRESH_TOKEN_SECRET: fc75593f45889b1e6fbd283ab846b36d0b6998b4954097f3e8fc4d8c6adb5807
          REFRESH_SECRET: fc75593f45889b1e6fbd283ab846b36d0b6998b4954097f3e8fc4d8c6adb5807

      - name: Build Application
        run: npm run build
        env:
          NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED: 1
          NODE_ENV: production
          NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL: https://app.innoventixhub.com
          DATABASE_URL: postgres://postgres:postgres_dev_password@localhost:54322/innoventix
          JWT_SECRET: d0a391b9da5876ead44bdbf4de07fa3cf73ebe0355f65521e9b902f256c4851f
          REFRESH_TOKEN_SECRET: fc75593f45889b1e6fbd283ab846b36d0b6998b4954097f3e8fc4d8c6adb5807
          REFRESH_SECRET: fc75593f45889b1e6fbd283ab846b36d0b6998b4954097f3e8fc4d8c6adb5807

  # =========================================================================
  # STEP 3 & 4: BUILD DOCKER IMAGE & PUSH TO GHCR
  # =========================================================================
  build-and-push:
    name: Build & Push Docker Image
    needs: validate
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      image_tag: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.version }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout Code
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Docker Buildx
        uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3

      - name: Log in to GitHub Container Registry (GHCR)
        uses: docker/login-action@v3
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      - name: Extract Docker Metadata
        id: meta
        uses: docker/metadata-action@v5
        with:
          images: ghcr.io/${{ github.repository }}
          tags: |
            type=raw,value=latest,enable=${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' }}
            type=sha,prefix=sha-,format=short
            type=raw,value=staging,enable=${{ github.event.inputs.target_env == 'staging' }}

      - name: Build and Push Docker Image
        uses: docker/build-push-action@v5
        with:
          context: .
          push: true
          tags: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.tags }}
          labels: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.labels }}
          cache-from: type=gha
          cache-to: type=gha,mode=max
          build-args: |
            NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL=https://app.innoventixhub.com


  # =========================================================================
  # STEP 5, 6 & 7: DEPLOY TO CONTABO VPS WITH POST-DEPLOY HEALTHCHECK & ROLLBACK
  # =========================================================================
  deploy:
    name: Deploy to Contabo VPS
    needs: build-and-push
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: SSH Deploy to Contabo VPS
        uses: appleboy/ssh-action@v1.0.3
        env:
          IMAGE_TAG: sha-${{ github.sha }}
          TARGET_ENV: ${{ github.event.inputs.target_env || 'production' }}
          REGISTRY_USER: ${{ github.actor }}
          REGISTRY_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          REPO_NAME: ${{ github.repository }}
        with:
          host: ${{ secrets.CONTABO_HOST }}
          username: ${{ secrets.CONTABO_USER }}
          key: ${{ secrets.CONTABO_SSH_KEY }}
          port: ${{ secrets.CONTABO_SSH_PORT || 22 }}
          envs: IMAGE_TAG,TARGET_ENV,REGISTRY_USER,REGISTRY_PASSWORD,REPO_NAME
          script_stop: true
          script: |
            set -euo pipefail

            echo "================================================================="
            echo " Starting Deployment on Contabo VPS"
            echo " Repository:  ${REPO_NAME}"
            echo " Image Tag:   ${IMAGE_TAG}"
            echo " Environment: ${TARGET_ENV}"
            echo " Timestamp:   $(date -u +'%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%SZ')"
            echo "================================================================="

            # 1. Authenticate Docker with GHCR
            echo "${REGISTRY_PASSWORD}" | docker login ghcr.io -u "${REGISTRY_USER}" --password-stdin

            # 2. Navigate to application deployment directory
            APP_DIR="/opt/innoventix/app"
            if [ ! -d "${APP_DIR}" ]; then
              echo "Error: Directory ${APP_DIR} does not exist on VPS!"
              exit 1
            fi
            cd "${APP_DIR}"

            FULL_IMAGE="ghcr.io/${REPO_NAME}:${IMAGE_TAG}"

            echo "==> Pulling new container image: ${FULL_IMAGE}..."
            docker pull "${FULL_IMAGE}"

            # 3. Configure target container and port
            if [ "${TARGET_ENV}" = "staging" ]; then
              CONTAINER_NAME="innoventix-app-staging"
              PORT=3005
              COMPOSE_SERVICE="app-staging"
              export APP_IMAGE_STAGING="${FULL_IMAGE}"
              COMPOSE_CMD="docker compose --profile staging up -d ${COMPOSE_SERVICE}"
            else
              CONTAINER_NAME="innoventix-app"
              PORT=3000
              COMPOSE_SERVICE="app"
              export APP_IMAGE="${FULL_IMAGE}"
              COMPOSE_CMD="docker compose up -d ${COMPOSE_SERVICE}"
            fi

            # 4. Identify previously running image for automatic rollback
            PREV_IMAGE=$(docker inspect --format='{{.Config.Image}}' "${CONTAINER_NAME}" 2>/dev/null || true)
            echo "==> Previously running image: ${PREV_IMAGE:-None}"

            # 5. Start new container
            echo "==> Starting updated container (${COMPOSE_SERVICE})..."
            eval "${COMPOSE_CMD}"

            # 6. Post-deploy health check (verify /api/health)
            echo "==> Verifying post-deploy health check on http://127.0.0.1:${PORT}/api/health..."
            HEALTHY=0
            for i in $(seq 1 15); do
              echo "Attempt $i of 15: Probing /api/health..."
              if curl -s -f "http://127.0.0.1:${PORT}/api/health" | grep -q '"status":"ok"'; then
                echo "==> Health check passed successfully!"
                HEALTHY=1
                break
              fi
              sleep 3
            done

            # 7. Automatic rollback if health check fails
            if [ "${HEALTHY}" -ne 1 ]; then
              echo "================================================================="
              echo " FATAL: Health check failed for ${FULL_IMAGE} on port ${PORT}!"
              echo " Initiating automatic rollback..."
              echo "================================================================="

              if [ -n "${PREV_IMAGE}" ]; then
                echo "==> Rolling back to previous image: ${PREV_IMAGE}..."
                if [ "${TARGET_ENV}" = "staging" ]; then
                  export APP_IMAGE_STAGING="${PREV_IMAGE}"
                else
                  export APP_IMAGE="${PREV_IMAGE}"
                fi
                eval "${COMPOSE_CMD}"
                echo "==> Rollback container restored."
              else
                echo "==> No previous image available for rollback."
              fi
              exit 1
            fi

            # 8. Post-deploy cleanup of older dangling images
            echo "==> Pruning dangling Docker images..."
            docker image prune -f --filter "until=72h" || true

            echo "================================================================="
            echo " Deployment of ${FULL_IMAGE} to ${TARGET_ENV} completed successfully!"
            echo "================================================================="

--- FILE: AGENTS.md ---
# AGENTS.md — Instructions for AI Coding Agents

Guidelines and execution protocols for AI coding agents (Antigravity, Cursor, Claude Code, Codex, Copilot).

---

## 🎯 Primary Project Objective: Supabase → PostgreSQL Migration

This repository (`crm-project-management-saas`) is undergoing a complete architectural refactor:
1. **Goal**: Remove Supabase dependency entirely; migrate to self-hosted PostgreSQL (Docker / Contabo VPS) with custom JWT-based authentication.
2. **Guidance Roadmap**: The complete 60-file roadmap is documented under `migration-postgres-60-files/migration-postgres/`.
3. **Execution Tracking**: Every execution step, reason, and validation status MUST be logged in `MIGRATION_EXECUTION_LOG.md` and `.agent-state.md`.

---

## 📜 Agent Operating Rules

### 1. Atomic Commits & Dual-Repository Immediate Push (MANDATORY)
- **Every change must be committed individually** with clear, descriptive commit messages adhering to Conventional Commits (e.g. `feat(...)`, `refactor(...)`, `fix(...)`, `docs(...)`).
- **MUST PUSH EVERY COMMIT TO BOTH REPOSITORIES IMMEDIATELY**:
  1. **Repo 1 (`origin`)**: `https://github.com/MaazzAlii/crm-project-management-saas.git`
  2. **Repo 2 (`deploy`)**: `https://github.com/Urk-Khan/Project-Management-CRM.git`
- `origin` is configured with dual push URLs, and agents must always ensure both remotes are updated:
  ```bash
  git push origin main && git push deploy main
  ```
- Both repositories belong to the user and must stay 100% in sync at all times with every commit.

### 2. Mandatory Work & State Logging
- Before and after every major step or phase, update `MIGRATION_EXECUTION_LOG.md` with:
  - **Timestamp**
  - **Phase / Task ID**
  - **Action Performed**
  - **Why it was performed (Rationale)**
  - **Files modified / created**
  - **Verification / Test Result**

### 3. Architecture & Security Standards
- Multi-tenancy must be strictly enforced at the application layer on every query/mutation (`organization_id`).
- All secret keys and database URLs must be kept in `.env.local` / environment variables — never committed.
- Auth must utilize secure HTTP-only cookies and bcrypt password hashing.

---

## 🚀 Quick Verification Commands

```bash
npm run lint
npm run build
npm test
```

--- FILE: DEPLOYMENT_CHECKLIST.md ---
# Production Deployment Checklist

## Pre-Deployment (48 hours before)

- [ ] All code merged to main branch
- [ ] All tests passing (unit, integration, E2E)
- [ ] Database migrations tested on staging
- [ ] Load testing completed (5000+ concurrent users)
- [ ] Security audit passed
- [ ] Backup procedures verified
- [ ] Rollback plan documented and tested

## Deployment Day

### 1. Final Verification (1 hour before)
- [ ] SSH access to Contabo server confirmed
- [ ] Staging environment fully tested
- [ ] Team on standby for monitoring
- [ ] Slack notifications configured

### 2. Deployment (Production Cutover)
- [ ] Stop old application (if exists)
- [ ] Push Docker image to registry
- [ ] Pull image on production server
- [ ] Run database migrations
- [ ] Start new application containers
- [ ] Verify health check endpoint: https://project-manager.calara.agency/api/health
- [ ] Test critical user flows (login, create org, CRM operations)

### 3. Post-Deployment (2 hours)
- [ ] Monitor error rates (should be < 1%)
- [ ] Monitor API latency (should be < 200ms p95)
- [ ] Monitor database connections (should be stable)
- [ ] Check backup jobs ran successfully
- [ ] Verify monitoring/alerting is active

### 4. Validation (24 hours)
- [ ] All users can log in
- [ ] Data integrity verified
- [ ] No duplicate records
- [ ] Email notifications working
- [ ] n8n automation webhooks firing
- [ ] Stripe webhooks processing correctly
- [ ] All audit logs created
- [ ] Performance metrics baseline established

## Rollback Procedure (if issues occur)

1. Restore previous database backup
2. Rollback Docker image to previous version
3. Restart application containers
4. Verify health check and critical flows
5. Notify team and users

## Post-Rollback

- [ ] Investigate root cause
- [ ] Fix issue on development
- [ ] Re-test thoroughly
- [ ] Schedule new deployment

# Tenant Isolation and Mock Data Audit Report

> **Audit Date:** 2026-10-10  
> **Target Branch:** `main` (Synced with `deploy/main` at commit `5c2c92f`)  
> **Scope:** Read-Only Audit of API Route Handlers, Server Actions, Server Components, Mock Data, and Navigation Routes.

---

## Executive Summary Table

| Item | Severity | File | Screen / Area Affected | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **A-1** | **CRITICAL** | `app/(dashboard)/projects/[id]/page.tsx` (L38) | Project Detail (`/projects/[id]`) | Unfiltered `SELECT id, full_name, email FROM users` queries and leaks all platform users across all tenants. |
| **A-2** | **CRITICAL** | `app/(dashboard)/projects/kanban/page.tsx` (L23) | Projects Kanban (`/projects/kanban`) | Unfiltered `SELECT id, name FROM clients` queries and leaks every client in the platform across all tenants. |
| **A-3** | **CRITICAL** | `app/(dashboard)/projects/kanban/page.tsx` (L24) | Projects Kanban (`/projects/kanban`) | Unfiltered `SELECT id, full_name, email FROM users` queries and leaks all users across all tenants. |
| **A-4** | **CRITICAL** | `app/api/users/route.ts` (L17) | Users API (`GET /api/users`) | Calls `userService.listUsers()` executing `SELECT * FROM users` without tenant scoping; any authenticated user can dump all platform users. |

### 2. Analytics Quotas: Computed vs Hardcoded Breakdown

Source: `lib/billing/plan-limits.ts:193–330` in `getOrganizationPlanUsageDetails(organizationId)`.

| Metric / Label | Display Value | Source | Computed from Database vs Hardcoded Fallback |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Plan Name** | `"Starter Plan"` | `organization_subscriptions` JOIN `subscription_plans` | **Database Query with Fallback**: Queries `sp.name FROM organization_subscriptions os JOIN subscription_plans sp ON sp.id = os.plan_id WHERE os.organization_id = $1`. If no subscription row exists, defaults to hardcoded `'Starter Plan'` (L316). |
| **Team Members** | `"1/5"` | `organization_members` COUNT & `feature_limits` | **Numerator is Computed, Denominator is Hardcoded/Plan**: Numerator computed via `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM organization_members WHERE organization_id = $1` (L230). Denominator comes from `sp.feature_limits.max_team_members` or hardcoded fallback `5` (L211). |
| **Projects** | `"0/50"` | `projects` COUNT & `feature_limits` | **Numerator is Computed, Denominator is Hardcoded/Plan**: Numerator computed via `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM projects WHERE organization_id = $1` (L232). Denominator comes from `sp.feature_limits.max_projects` or hardcoded fallback `50` (L213). |
| **Connected Channels** | `"0/1"` | `communication_channels` COUNT & `feature_limits` | **Numerator is Computed, Denominator is Hardcoded/Plan**: Numerator computed via `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM communication_channels WHERE organization_id = $1 AND status = 'active'` (L233). Denominator comes from `sp.feature_limits.communication_channels_included` or hardcoded fallback `1` (L217). |
| **Cloud Storage** | `"0.2 / 10 GB"` | Synthetic Formula | **Synthetic Formula**: Computed as `Math.max(0.2, ((projects * 5 + clients * 2) / 100))` (L244–247). Denominator is hardcoded fallback `10 GB`. |

### 3. Client Card "Connected" Badge Breakdown

1. **Originating Source**: Rendered by `components/clients/CommunicationModeBadge.tsx` and used within `components/clients/ClientsList.tsx` (L368, L432) and `components/leads/DealCard.tsx` (L146).
2. **Database Column**: Backed by `clients.communication_mode` (`'manual'` or `'connected'`).
3. **Logic**:
   ```tsx
   const isConnected = mode === 'connected'
   if (isConnected) {
     return (
       <span className="... border-emerald-500/30 bg-emerald-500/10 text-emerald-400" title="Connected Hub: Auto-syncs conversations from linked channels into unified inbox">
         <Radio className="h-3 w-3 animate-pulse" />
         <span>Connected</span>
       </span>
     )
   }
   ```
4. **Analysis of "rahmat" Client and "Connected" Badge**:
   - Investigation reveals that the "Connected" badge on client cards like "rahmat" is **NOT fake mock data**.
   - In `components/clients/ClientForm.tsx` (L30–46), the form state initializes with:
     - `platform: 'WhatsApp'`
     - `communication_mode: initialMode` (where `initialMode = 'connected'` by default).
   - When a user/tester creates a real client (such as "rahmat") and only fills in the name without modifying these dropdowns, the form submits `communication_mode: 'connected'` and `platform: 'WhatsApp'`.
   - The server action `createClientAction` saves these values to the Postgres database.
   - When `/clients` is loaded, it reads this real record from Postgres and renders the `<CommunicationModeBadge mode="connected" />` and the `'WhatsApp'` badge.
   - Therefore, the "Connected" badge represents real user-created data in the database, not hardcoded mock strings. The empty area on the "rahmat" card is caused by `ClientsList.tsx` (L442–461) rendering empty contact dividers when email, phone, and country are omitted.

## Part D: Test Coverage Analysis

### Evaluation of Existing Test Suites Against CRITICAL Vulnerabilities

The codebase contains 24 Vitest unit/integration tests and 7 Playwright E2E spec files.

| CRITICAL Leak | File & Line | Would Existing Unit/Integration Tests Catch This? | Would Existing Playwright Tests Catch This? | Explanation of Test Blind Spot |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **All Platform Users Leaked in Project Detail** | `app/(dashboard)/projects/[id]/page.tsx:38` | **NO** | **NO** | Vitest tests do not mount or render server component page files. E2E tests (`project-lifecycle.spec.ts`) only run within a single logged-in session and verify that the page renders without testing if other organization users appear in the assignee select. |
| **All Platform Clients Leaked in Kanban** | `app/(dashboard)/projects/kanban/page.tsx:23` | **NO** | **NO** | Vitest tests mock repository methods and do not execute the inline raw SQL query in `kanban/page.tsx`. E2E tests have no assertions verifying client multi-tenancy isolation. |
| **All Platform Users Leaked in Kanban** | `app/(dashboard)/projects/kanban/page.tsx:24` | **NO** | **NO** | Same as above. E2E tests only verify that the Kanban board renders columns. |
| **Unrestricted User List API** | `app/api/users/route.ts:17` | **NO** | **NO** | `tests/phase5-api-services.test.ts` tests `userService` in isolation without verifying that the HTTP route handler enforces an organization boundary. E2E tests do not call `/api/users`. |
| **Cross-Tenant User Profile Read** | `app/api/users/[id]/route.ts:17` | **NO** | **NO** | No negative cross-tenant authorization tests exist for user profile routes. |
| **Cross-Tenant Team Members Leak** | `app/api/organizations/[id]/members/route.ts:17` | **NO** | **NO** | Vitest tests for organizations do not attempt cross-tenant ID access against the route handler. |
| **Cross-Tenant Organization Details Leak** | `app/api/organizations/[id]/route.ts:17` | **NO** | **NO** | No cross-tenant negative test exists for `GET /api/organizations/[id]`. |
| **Query Parameter Tenant Hijacking** | `app/api/crm/*` & `app/api/projects/*` | **NO** | **NO** | Tests only supply valid default auth objects and never test injecting a malicious `?orgId=` parameter to probe cross-tenant access. |

### Summary of Testing Gaps
1. **No Negative Security Tests**: Zero tests in Vitest or Playwright attempt to access Resource B belonging to Tenant B while authenticated as Tenant A.
2. **Server Components Completely Untested for Tenancy**: Server components containing direct SQL queries (`projects/[id]/page.tsx`, `projects/kanban/page.tsx`) have zero unit or integration test coverage.
3. **Heavy Mocking in Vitest**: Tests like `tests/rls-isolation.test.ts` test a JavaScript imitation model rather than actual running application routes or database queries.

# Transactional Email Deliverability Guide

This checklist details the DNS records and validation practices required for the primary sending domain (`EMAIL_FROM_ADDRESS`, e.g. `innoventix.io`).

> **Note for Company Administrator**: AI Coding Agents do not configure production DNS records. The administrator must publish these records directly in the company's DNS dashboard (e.g. Cloudflare, AWS Route53).

---

## 1. SPF (Sender Policy Framework) Record
An SPF record lists all servers authorized to send email on behalf of your domain.

- **Record Type**: `TXT`
- **Host**: `@` (or the specific subdomain if sending from e.g. `mail.innoventix.io`)
- **Value**:
  ```text
  v=spf1 mx a:mail.innoventix.io -all
  ```
- **Rule**: If you utilize multiple mail relays (e.g. Google Workspace alongside Mailcow), combine them within a single TXT record:
  ```text
  v=spf1 mx a:mail.innoventix.io include:_spf.google.com -all
  ```
- **Failure Policy**: Avoid `~all` (softfail) once testing is complete; use `-all` (hardfail) to prevent spoofing.

---

## 2. DKIM (DomainKeys Identified Mail) Record
DKIM attaches a cryptographic signature to every outgoing email, verified by receiving mail servers against your published public key.

- **Record Type**: `TXT`
- **Host / Selector**: `<selector>._domainkey` (e.g. `dkim._domainkey` or `mailcow._domainkey`)
- **Value**:
  ```text
  v=DKIM1; k=rsa; p=MIIBIjANBgkqhkiG9w0BAQEFAAOCAQ8AMIIBCgKCAQEA...
  ```
- **Key Length**: Always use a 2048-bit RSA key.
- **Provider Alignment**: The DKIM key must be generated in the Mailcow admin UI (**Configuration** > **ARC/DKIM**) for the sending domain.

---

## 3. DMARC (Domain-based Message Authentication, Reporting & Conformance)
DMARC protects domain reputation by instructing receivers how to handle emails that fail SPF or DKIM.

- **Record Type**: `TXT`
- **Host**: `_dmarc`
- **Starting Value (Monitoring Mode)**:
  ```text
  v=DMARC1; p=none; rua=mailto:dmarc-reports@innoventix.io; ruf=mailto:dmarc-reports@innoventix.io; sp=none; aspf=r; adkim=r
  ```
- **Gradual Enforcement**:
  1. **Phase 1 (Monitoring)**: `p=none` for 2–4 weeks while inspecting XML aggregate reports sent to `rua`.
  2. **Phase 2 (Quarantine)**: `p=quarantine; pct=25` graduating to `pct=100` once legitimate senders are confirmed.
  3. **Phase 3 (Rejection)**: `p=reject` for total protection against domain spoofing.

---

## 4. Human-Monitored Reply-To Address
Transactional emails that bounce or receive user inquiries must never lead to a dead end.

- **Default Reply-To**: Set `EMAIL_REPLY_TO=support@innoventix.io` to a shared inbox monitored by support team members.
- **Inviter Override**: When an organization member has a verified email (`email_verified = true`), platform invitation emails route replies directly to that inviter. If unverified, the system falls back safely to `EMAIL_REPLY_TO`.

---

## 5. End-to-End Verification Checklist

| Step | Action | Success Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **1. CLI Delivery Test** | Run `npx tsx scripts/send-test-email.ts <dest>` | Exits with `0` and returns SMTP `messageId` |
| **2. Gmail Inspection** | Send to personal `@gmail.com` address | Primary Inbox placement; "Show Original" confirms `SPF: PASS`, `DKIM: PASS`, `DMARC: PASS` |
| **3. Outlook Inspection** | Send to personal `@outlook.com` address | Focused Inbox placement; Message source shows `Authentication-Results: ... dkim=pass header.i=@innoventix.io` |
| **4. Spam Score Benchmark** | Send to [mail-tester.com](https://www.mail-tester.com) | Score **9.0 / 10** or higher |
| **5. Reverse DNS (PTR)** | Contabo VPS reverse DNS check | Reverse PTR for the Mailcow IP resolves to `mail.innoventix.io` |

--- FILE: docs/email-setup.md ---
# Transactional Email Setup & Configuration

This guide details the configuration variables and DNS requirements for Innoventix team invitations and transactional email delivery.

---

## 1. Environment Variables Reference

| Variable | Provider | Purpose | Example Value |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `EMAIL_PROVIDER` | All | Selects active transactional mail transport (`console`, `resend`, or `smtp`) | `resend` / `smtp` / `console` |
| `EMAIL_FROM` | All | Default platform From header address | `Innoventix <invites@your-domain.com>` |
| `APP_PUBLIC_URL` | All | Base URL for invite links and verification callbacks | `https://project-manager.calara.agency` |
| `RESEND_API_KEY` | `resend` | Secret API key generated in Resend Dashboard | `re_123456789...` |
| `SMTP_HOST` | `smtp` | Outgoing SMTP server hostname | `smtp.mailcow.email` / `smtp.sendgrid.net` |
| `SMTP_PORT` | `smtp` | Outgoing SMTP server port | `587` (STARTTLS) or `465` (SSL) |
| `SMTP_USER` | `smtp` | SMTP username / mailbox address | `invites@your-domain.com` |
| `SMTP_PASSWORD` | `smtp` | SMTP password / app password | `secret_smtp_password` |

---

## 2. Environment Behavior & Safety Rules

- **Development (`NODE_ENV=development`)**:
  - `EMAIL_PROVIDER` defaults to `console`.
  - Invitation and verification emails (including raw activation links) print directly to server output logs.
- **Production (`NODE_ENV=production`)**:
  - `EMAIL_PROVIDER=console` is **strictly refused**. The application throws a startup validation error if `console` is selected or if credentials for `resend` or `smtp` are missing.

---

## 3. Sender Name & From Address Rule

- For team invitations, the sender display name shows the **inviting organization name** (e.g. `Acme Corp via Innoventix`).
- The actual RFC From address **always remains the platform's domain** (e.g. `<invites@your-domain.com>`).
- This guarantees that outbound emails pass SPF and DKIM alignment checks regardless of tenant organization names.

---

## 4. DNS Configuration: SPF, DKIM, and DMARC

To guarantee deliverability and prevent emails from landing in spam or being rejected, configure the following DNS records for the domain matching `EMAIL_FROM`:

### 1. SPF (Sender Policy Framework)
- **Type**: `TXT`
- **Host**: `@` (or subdomain)
- **Value**: `v=spf1 include:resend.com ~all` (or your SMTP relay provider)

### 2. DKIM (DomainKeys Identified Mail)
- Configure the CNAME / TXT keys provided by your mail provider (e.g. Resend or Mailcow) in your domain DNS zone.

### 3. DMARC
- **Type**: `TXT`
- **Host**: `_dmarc`
- **Value**: `v=DMARC1; p=quarantine; pct=100; rua=mailto:dmarc-reports@your-domain.com`

## 🚀 Coolify Configuration Matrix

### 1. Required, Set in Coolify Application Settings
These variables must be explicitly defined in Coolify for the production web container:
- `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL` (e.g. `https://www.project-manager.calara.agency`)

- `NODE_ENV=production`

### 2. Required, Generated Per Environment (Secrets)
Generate strong 32+ byte random hex strings for each environment:
- `DATABASE_URL` (e.g. `postgresql://postgres:<GENERATED_DB_PASSWORD>@postgres:5432/innoventix`)
- `JWT_SECRET` (generate via `openssl rand -hex 32`)
- `REFRESH_TOKEN_SECRET` (generate via `openssl rand -hex 32`)
- `ENCRYPTION_SECRET` (generate via `openssl rand -hex 32`)

- `CRON_SECRET`
- `EMAIL_FROM`
- `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY`
- `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`
- `OPENAI_API_KEY`
- `GEMINI_API_KEY`
- `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN`

- `DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN`

- `N8N_WEBHOOK_URL`
- `N8N_WEBHOOK_SECRET`

### 4. Do NOT Set in Production (Script / Dev-Only)
The following variables are strictly for local testing or CI scripts and should **never** be injected into Coolify production containers:
- `ALLOW_DEV_AUTH_BYPASS` (Must remain false/unset in production)
- `DEV_SUPER_ADMIN` (Must remain false/unset in production)
- `TEST_BASE_URL` (Local Playwright script test URL)
- `TEST_USER_EMAIL` (Local script test user)
- `TEST_USER_PASSWORD` (Local script test password)
- `LIVE_DOMAIN_URL` (Screenshot verification script target)
- `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL` (Legacy test script artifact)
- `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` (Legacy test script artifact)

--- FILE: docs/invite-email-rules.md ---
# Team Invitation Email Rules & Architecture

Guidelines for team invitations and transactional notifications in Innoventix Hub.

---

## 1. Sender Identity & Domain Alignment

- **From Address**: Always sent from the official platform mailbox (`EMAIL_FROM_ADDRESS`, e.g. `invites@innoventix.io`). Invitations are never sent from personal addresses or an inviter's private mailbox. This guarantees strict SPF and DKIM authentication alignment.
- **Display Name**: Displays as `"{Inviter name} via Innoventix"` (e.g. `Maaz Ali via Innoventix`), ensuring the invitee immediately recognizes who invited them. System alerts (email confirmation, domain codes) use the platform name alone.
- **Reply-To**: Set to the inviter's email address **only if** their email is verified. If unverified, it falls back to the platform support mailbox (`EMAIL_REPLY_TO`, e.g. `support@innoventix.io`).

## 2. Content & Privacy Standards

- **Plain-Text Version**: Every outgoing email must contain both HTML and plain-text versions.
- **Security & Token Safety**: Emails never expose database IDs, passwords, or token hashes. They contain only the secure one-time redemption link and expiration date.
- **XSS Protection**: All user-supplied strings (names, company names) are automatically HTML-escaped.
- **Legitimacy Notice**: Every invitation email includes the standard security disclaimer: *"If you did not expect this, ignore this email."*

## 3. Email Templates Summary

| Template | Purpose | Subject Format | Expiry |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Team Invite** | Invite a colleague to a workspace | `{Inviter} invited you to {Organization} on Innoventix` | 7 Days |
| **Verify Email** | Account email confirmation | `Confirm your email` | 24 Hours |
| **Domain Code** | Business domain verification | `Your domain verification code` | 30 Minutes |
| **Invite Accepted**| Alert inviter that invitee joined | `{Member} joined {Organization}` | N/A |
| **Role Changed** | Alert member of role modification | `Your role in {Organization} was updated` | N/A |

--- FILE: docs/mailcow-email-setup.md ---
# Mailcow Email Setup & Administrator Runbook

This guide details the steps required for the company administrator to configure, verify, and monitor Mailcow SMTP for transactional platform emails (such as team invitations, email verification, and workspace notifications).

---

## 1. Mailcow Mailbox Provisioning
1. Log in to the Mailcow UI at your Contabo server (e.g. `https://mail.innoventix.io`).
2. Navigate to **Configuration** > **Mailboxes**.
3. Create the dedicated platform application mailbox:
   - **Email Address**: `invites@innoventix.io` (or `noreply@innoventix.io`)
   - **Display Name**: `Innoventix Platform`
   - **Password**: Generate a high-entropy 32+ character random password.
4. Save the credentials securely in the production `.env.local` / Coolify environment variables:
   ```env
   EMAIL_PROVIDER=smtp
   SMTP_HOST=mail.innoventix.io
   SMTP_PORT=587
   SMTP_SECURE=false
   SMTP_USER=invites@innoventix.io
   SMTP_PASS="<GENERATED_PASSWORD>"
   EMAIL_FROM_ADDRESS=invites@innoventix.io
   EMAIL_FROM_NAME="Innoventix"
   EMAIL_REPLY_TO=support@innoventix.io
   APP_PUBLIC_URL=https://app.innoventix.io
   ```

---

## 2. DKIM Key Generation
1. In Mailcow, navigate to **Configuration** > **ARC/DKIM**.
2. Select your sending domain (e.g. `innoventix.io`).
3. Set **Key size**: `2048` bits.
4. Set **Selector**: `dkim` (or `mailcow`).
5. Click **Generate** and copy the resulting public key record.

---

## 3. DNS Configuration for Sending Domain
Publish the following DNS records at your DNS provider (e.g. Cloudflare, Route53, Namecheap):

### A. SPF (Sender Policy Framework)
Add or update the TXT record on the root domain (`innoventix.io`):
```text
Type: TXT
Name: @
Value: v=spf1 mx a:mail.innoventix.io -all
```
*(If other authorized senders exist, include them, e.g. `include:_spf.google.com`)*

### B. DKIM (DomainKeys Identified Mail)
Add the TXT record for the selector generated in Step 2:
```text
Type: TXT
Name: dkim._domainkey
Value: v=DKIM1; k=rsa; p=MIIBIjANBgkqhkiG9w0BAQEFAAOCAQ8AMIIBCgKCAQEA...
```

### C. DMARC (Domain-based Message Authentication)
Add the TXT record for `_dmarc`:
```text
Type: TXT
Name: _dmarc
Value: v=DMARC1; p=none; rua=mailto:dmarc-reports@innoventix.io; ruf=mailto:dmarc-reports@innoventix.io; sp=none; aspf=r; adkim=r
```
*Note: Start in monitoring mode (`p=none`). Transition to quarantine (`p=quarantine`) or reject (`p=reject`) after verifying zero legitimate email drops.*

---

## 4. Firewall & Connectivity Verification
Verify that outbound TCP traffic on port `587` is open from the Coolify application container to Mailcow:
```bash
# Test connectivity from application server / container:
nc -zv mail.innoventix.io 587
# Or via curl:
curl -v telnet://mail.innoventix.io:587
```

---

## 5. Send Test Message via CLI Script
Innoventix provides a dedicated test utility to verify SMTP credentials and deliverability without touching the web UI:

```bash
npx tsx scripts/send-test-email.ts <admin-destination@example.com>
```

### Script Behavior:
- Dispatches a single multipart email (HTML + Plain-Text).
- Uses strict TLS certificate validation (`rejectUnauthorized: true`).
- Logs the returned SMTP `messageId` on success.
- Formats typed error codes without ever leaking the password.

---

## 6. Inbox & Header Deliverability Inspection
1. Send test messages to both a **Gmail** and an **Outlook/Office 365** mailbox:
   ```bash
   npx tsx scripts/send-test-email.ts your.name@gmail.com
   npx tsx scripts/send-test-email.ts your.name@outlook.com
   ```
2. In Gmail, open the message > Click three dots (More) > **Show original**:
   - Check **SPF**: `PASS` with IP of Mailcow server.
   - Check **DKIM**: `PASS` with domain `innoventix.io`.
   - Check **DMARC**: `PASS`.
3. In Outlook, view Message Source and confirm the same `Authentication-Results` headers.
4. Verify the email lands in the Primary inbox, NOT the Spam / Junk folder.

---

## 7. Deliverability Scoring at mail-tester.com
1. Visit [mail-tester.com](https://www.mail-tester.com) to get a unique sink email address (e.g. `test-xxxx@srv1.mail-tester.com`).
2. Dispatch a test message:
   ```bash
   npx tsx scripts/send-test-email.ts test-xxxx@srv1.mail-tester.com
   ```
3. Check score on mail-tester.com.
4. **Target score**: **9.5/10 or 10/10** before opening user invitations to external parties.
